source.title: Hijacking Large Language Models via Adversarial In-Context Learning
source.authors: Xiang-Yu Zhou; Yao Qiang; S. Z. Zade; Prashant Khanduri; Dong-Xiao Zhu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Table 3 is flattened in places, so some model-by-condition values cannot be assigned confidently.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether adversarial suffixes can elicit harmful responses from safeguarded chat models, using gradient-optimized suffixes in in-context demonstrations rather than the other bypass methods named in V4.
record.gate_note: The study also reports attacks on sentiment classification, but those outcomes are not harmful-request refusal behavior. It does not measure fine-tuning, per-token KL, weight localization, or safety-training depth.
record.test_reason: The study reports refusal-bypass rates (ASR) on AdvBench harmful queries for three safety-tuned chat models. The attack appends gradient-optimized suffixes to harmful in-context demos, a new input-side bypass setting bearing on V4. ASR is keyword-based: it counts responses that lack refusal phrases.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that gradient-optimized suffixes on in-context demos hijack LLMs, including bypassing safety guardrails to elicit harmful responses, by diverting attention to the suffixes. They also conclude that adding clean demos at test time mitigates the attack, with Suf. strongest on jailbreaks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient-guided adversarial suffixes appended to in-context demonstrations and evaluates harmful-response ASR; it does not fine-tune models or measure response-position KL.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies with the number and ordering of in-context demos; the authors report stronger attack susceptibility with more demos, and different effects for prefix versus suffix placement of clean defense demos.

fits_no_version.finding: GGI suffixes on in-context demos force target sentiment or topic labels: negative-class accuracy collapses to near 0 on SST-2, RT and AG's News (Tables 1, 2, 5, 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimized demo suffixes hijack ICL classification outputs regardless of the query.

record.problems: The paper provides no uncertainty estimates for the reported ASRs. Table 3 is flattened in the supplied text, preventing confident assignment of several model-by-condition attack values. The zero-shot Mistral ASR is not a matched no-defense baseline for the reported defended GGI results.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3's per-model, per-attack, per-shot ASR and defense values were not extracted where the flattened layout did not support confident assignment. The text's explicit Mistral Suf. values and zero-shot values are retained in r4–r8.

untested.parts: Prefilling a compliant response opening and decoding changes. The attack instead puts compliant answers inside in-context demos, plus optimized suffixes on those demos. No check of harmfulness beyond the absence of refusal phrases.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No analysis of why safety is shallow.

missing.what: Full Table 3 jailbreak ASRs for the baseline attacks (ICA, Square, Greedy) per model and shot setting. Example: ICA on Mistral is 93.7/97.5, while baselines on LLaMA3.1 are ≤1.5.
ASR under the Instruction (system-prompt) defense and the Pre. defense. Example: GGI on Vicuna at 4-shot is 97.8 with Instruction and 86.0 with Pre.; on LLaMA3.1 at 4-shot, 43.4 and 66.4.
Separate rows for 2-shot and 4-shot GGI ASR per model, plus the Suf. defense rows for Vicuna and LLaMA3.1.

record.verdict_notes: Success is defined only by the absence of refusal phrases, so ASR measures non-refusal, not verified harmfulness. The jailbreak demos already contain compliant 'Sure, here are...' answers, so the attack mixes harmful in-context demonstrations with optimized suffixes. The test-set size is inconsistent: Table 4 and Section 6.3 say 1,000 queries, while the appendix text says 200. No uncertainty is reported. The Table 3 flattening was resolvable: the Suf. values 4.9 and 8.6 match the text.

versions.untested_parts: Tests adversarial suffixes appended to in-context demos; does not test a prefilled compliant opening or decoding changes.
Does not test whether the data or objective produces shallow safety.
No training to deepen safety or evaluation of whether deepening holds up.
